readme_excerpt:
# AI Pose Gallery · 中文版

> 288 组 / 1439 张 AI 人体姿势参考图，日文数据完整汉化，附可直接部署的响应式静态画廊。

![画廊预览](docs/preview.jpg)

<details><summary>手机端预览</summary>

![手机端预览](docs/mobile.jpg)

</details>

**在线演示：** <https://ai-pose-gallery.anhao.app/>
**原始站点：** <https://ai-pose-gallery.pages.dev/>
**原作者：** ギア（@giaaibusi）
**中文版维护：** Anhao · [X @anhao_ai](https://x.com/anhao_ai)
**GitHub：** <https://github.com/anhao/ai-pose-gallery-zh>

---

## 这是什么

原站是一套面向 AI 绘画 / 3D / 摄影参考的姿势图库，元数据全部为日文，且不提供批量素材下载。本仓库做了三件事：

1. **全量镜像** —— 1439 条记录对应的 1439 张缩略图（JPG 300×400）与 1439 张原图（PNG 900×1200）全部落地，共 2878 个文件 / 659.5 MB。
2. **完整汉化** —— 日文字段逐条译为中文，覆盖 4 个体系、26 个分类、288 个姿势名、5 个视角，零遗漏。
3. **可用的前端** —— 零依赖响应式画廊，完整实现原站的分类筛选、多角度切换、分组浏览、灯箱导航与原图下载，并针对手机重新设计布局。

## 页面功能

- 4 个体系页签，显示各体系的图片数与姿势组数
- 姿势名、编号、ID、分类关键词搜索，支持 `/` 快速聚焦
- 动作分类、5 种视角组合筛选，可一键重置
- **按姿势分组 / 逐张浏览**双模式，分组卡片带多角度缩略图
- 悬停或点击缩略图切换主图角度，点击卡片打开灯箱
- 灯箱先显示缩略图、再加载 900×1200 原图，支持直接下载 PNG、复制 ID、新窗口打开
- `← / →` 切换角度，`↑ / ↓` 切换姿势，`Esc` 关闭；手机支持左右滑动
- PC 多列网格、手机双列网格，移动端筛选面板可展开/收起
- 使用指南与注意事项弹窗，页脚标注图片来源与维护者链接

## SEO 与分享

页面内置了完整的 SEO 与社交分享配置：

- 关键词化标题：`AI 姿势参考库｜288 组人体姿势 · 1439 张多角度参考图`
- 独立 description、keywords、author 与 `max-image-preview:large`
- `canonical` 指向正式域名，避免自定义域名与 pages.dev 域名重复收录
- Open Graph / Twitter Card 使用 1200×630 的 `og-cover.jpg`
- JSON-LD 结构化数据：`WebSite` + `ImageGallery`，声明语言、简介与页面主图
- `robots.txt` 放行全站并声明 sitemap，`sitemap.xml` 指向首页
- 语义结构：单一 H1、分区 H2、卡片 H3；缩略图 `alt` 含姿势名与视角，图片懒加载

仓库中的绝对地址统一指向 `https://ai-pose-gallery.anhao.app/`。Fork 后如使用其他域名，需同步替换 `index.html` 的 canonical、`og:*`、`twitter:*`、JSON-LD，以及 `robots.txt`、`sitemap.xml` 中的地址。

## 数据规模

| 体系 | 条数 |
| --- | ---: |
| 全身单人・标准系 | 365 |
| 全身单人・性感系 | 399 |
| 上半身单人 | 400 |
| 双人缠绵 | 275 |
| **合计** | **1439** |

每条记录对应 5 个视角中的若干个：正面 / 斜侧 / 侧面 / 俯视 / 仰视。

## 目录结构

```
.
├── index.html              # 单页画廊（零依赖，直接打开即可）
├── robots.txt              # 搜索引擎抓取规则
├── sitemap.xml             # 站点地图
├── og-cover.jpg            # 1200×630 社交分享封面
├── data/
│   ├── pose.json           # 原始日文数据（1439 条，未改动）
│   ├── pose-zh.json        # 中文数据（前端实际读取，含检索字段）
│   ├── meta.json           # 原始体系分类
│   ├── meta-zh.json        # 中文体系分类
│   └── translations.csv    # 日⇄中对照表（323 条，便于校对）
├── thumbs/                 # 缩略图 1439 张 JPG 300×400（22 MB）
├── img/                    # 原图 1439 张 PNG 900×1200（637 MB）
├── scripts/
│   ├── download.py         # 并发下载器（48 线程 / 断点续传 / 自动重试）
│   ├── i18n.py             # 日译中词典（唯一值去重后的 323 条译文）
│   ├── apply_translation.py# 回填译文，生成中文数据
│   ├── verify.py           # 校验文件完整性（存在性 / 大小 / 图片头）
│   └── build.sh            # 生成 Cloudflare Pages 发布目录 dist/
├── docs/                   # README 页面预览图
├── _headers                # Cloudflare Pages 缓存策略
├── LICENSE
└── README.md
```

## 数据结构

`data/pose-zh.json` 字段说明：

| 字段 | 原日文字段 | 示例 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | — | `full_sexy_P001_front` | 唯一标识 |
| `体系` | `系統` | 全身单人・性感系 | 4 大类 |
| `姿势编号` | `ポーズ番号` | `P001` | 80 组编号 |
| `分类` | `分類` | 站姿 | 26 类动作 |
| `姿势名称` | `ポーズ名` | S形站姿・胯部侧顶 | 288 种描述 |
| `角度` | `アングル` | 正面 | 5 种视角 |
| `缩略图` | `サムネ` | `thumbs/…jpg` | 相对路径 |
| `原图` | `原寸` | `img/…png` | 相对路径 |
| `检索` | — | 拼接串 | 供前端模糊搜索 |

原始日文数据 `data/pose.json` 保持原样，字段名与站点接口一致，便于对照或回灌。

## 本地预览

画廊通过 `fetch` 读取 JSON，需要 HTTP 环境（直接双击 `index.html` 会被 CORS 拦截）：

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 打开 http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

页面支持体系/分类/视角组合筛选、关键词搜索、分组与逐张浏览、多角度缩略图、懒加载、灯箱原图下载、键盘与触屏导航。

## 脚本用法

```bash
# 重新拉取全部图片（已存在的文件自动跳过，可反复执行）
python3 scripts/download.py
WORKERS=64 python3 scripts/download.py   # 调整并发

# 修改 scripts/i18n.py 中的译文后，重新生成中文数据
python3 scripts/apply_translation.py

# 校验 2878 个文件是否完整
python3 scripts/verify.py
```

## 部署到 Cloudflare Pages

仓库为纯静态站点，无框架、无依赖。

**方式一：GitHub 自动部署（推荐）**

1. 登录 Cloudflare Dashboard → **Workers & Pages** → **Create** → **Pages** → **Connect to Git**
2. 选择本仓库 → 生产分支 `main`
3. 构建设置照抄：

   | 字段 | 值 |
   | --- | --- |
   | Framework preset | `None` |
   | Build command | `bash scripts/build.sh` |
   | Build output directory | `dist` |

description: The agent skills I use every day. Works with Claude Code and Codex.
readme_excerpt:
# tstack

The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them. They work
in Claude Code and Codex. Some use [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)
features when they are available and fall back to native tools when they are
not.

## Skills

| Skill | Say | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `full-send` | "full send" | Takes a change to a merged PR with nobody watching: proves it, reviews it, files it, babysits it, merges it. |
| `full-stop` | "full stop" | Same as `full-send`, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge. |
| `council` | "council" | Gets review from three models from different providers, and loops until they agree. |
| `sol-loop` | "sol loop" | Reviews a change with GPT Sol in a loop until both agents agree. |
| `file-pr` | "file a PR" | Files a short PR that leads with the problem, not an inventory of changes. |
| `takeover` | "take over" | Finishes someone else's PR, branch, or agent thread, and keeps their credit. |
| `babysit-pr` | "babysit" | Watches a PR through CI and review bots, and fixes the real findings. |
| `modernize` | "modernize" | Rebases an old PR and decides if it should still exist. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | (automatic) | Formats comments that an agent posts on your behalf. |

Some skills call others. Install the ones they need too:

- `full-send` uses `sol-loop`, `file-pr`, and `babysit-pr`.
- `full-stop` uses `full-send`.
- `takeover` uses `modernize`, `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `leaving-pr-comments`.
- `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `modernize` use `leaving-pr-comments`.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/   # Claude Code
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.codex/skills/    # Codex
```

## Requirements

- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`).
- `python3` for `babysit-pr`'s `pr-wait` script.
- `council` and `sol-loop` need subagents on other providers' models. T3 Code
  does this with `delegate_task`. Otherwise you need a harness that can run
  those models.

## Make them yours

These are starting points. Edit them. Put personal settings, like which models
sit on your council, in your `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, so you can update the
skills without losing them.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

description: Agent Skills that teach coding agents to write, review, and port idiomatic Rust, plus a tested clippy config. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.
readme_excerpt: # Beautiful Rust Three standard [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) and a lints config that teach coding agents to write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Rust: - **`rust-best-practices`** loads whenever an agent writes or changes Rust, and steers it toward idiomatic, robust, maintainable code. - **`rust-review`** reviews existing Rust code, a file, a crate, or a diff, and writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix. - **`rust-port`** ports C, C++, Python, Go, or JavaScript to idiomatic Rust with the same behavior, porting the original tests first so you can prove the two match. - **`lints/`** is a drop-in clippy configuration that enforces the machine-checkable rules in CI. They work with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and any other agent that reads the Agent Skills format. Every code example in the skills compiles on stable Rust, and every lint in the config was checked against current clippy. The guidance is distilled from five sources, with a condensed digest of each bundled in the skill so the agent can consult the original reasoning when it needs to: - [Google Rust Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/rustguide.html) - [Rust API Guidelines](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/) (official rust-lang checklist) - [Effective Rust](https://www.lurklurk.org/effective-rust/) by David Drysdale - [Rust Design Patterns](https://rust-unofficial.github.io/patterns/) (idioms, patterns, anti-patterns) - [Microsoft Pragmatic Rust Guidelines](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/) Where the sources disagree, the skill picks a side and says why. ## What it changes Asked for a small semver-parsing library, an agent without the skill produced working code with public fields, no `# Errors` docs, and `unwrap()` in its doc examples. With the skill, the same agent kept the fields private, documented failure modes, and wrote doc examples users can copy safely. Condensed from those two runs: ```rust // Without the skill /// A semantic version. The fields are public for convenience. pub struct Version { pub major: u64, pub minor: u64, pub patch: u64, pub pre: Vec, pub build: Vec, } impl Version { /// Parses a version string. /// /// ``` /// let v = Version::parse("1.2.3").unwrap(); /// ``` pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result { /* ... */ } } ``` ```rust // With the skill /// A semantic version. Equality, hashing, and ordering ignore build metadata. pub struct Version { major: u64, minor: u64, patch: u64, pre: Vec, build: Vec, } impl Version { /// Parses a version string according to SemVer 2.0.0. /// /// # Errors /// /// Returns [`ParseVersionError`] if the string is empty, a numeric part has a /// leading zero or overflows `u64`, or an identifier contains invalid characters. /// /// ``` /// # use semver_lite::Version; /// # fn main() -> Result<(), semver_lite::ParseVersionError> { /// let v = Version::parse("1.2.3-beta.1")?; /// assert_eq!(v.major(), 1); /// # Ok(()) /// # } /// ``` pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result { /* ... */ } /// Returns the major version number. pub fn major(&self) -> u64 { self.major } } ``` Across three test tasks (a library, a CLI, and refactoring a messy module), the skill passed 29 of 30 checks against 24 of 30 without it. See [Testing the skills](#testing-the-skills). ## Install Each skill is a folder under `skills/`: `rust-best-practices/`, `rust-review/`, and `rust-port/`. Every option below puts those folders where your agent looks fo

description: Evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code): church books, civil, military, deportation and repression records across the former USSR. Replies in your language.
readme_excerpt:
# ex-USSR Kinship Research

![ex-USSR Kinship Research cover](docs/cover.jpg)

Languages: [English](README.md) / [Русский](README.ru.md) / [Беларуская](README.be.md) / [Қазақша](README.kk.md) / [Українська](README.uk.md) / [Polski](README.pl.md) / [Deutsch](README.de.md) / [Română](README.ro.md) / [Eesti](README.et.md) / [Latviešu](README.lv.md) / [Lietuvių](README.lt.md) / [ქართული](README.ka.md) / [Հայերեն](README.hy.md) / [Azərbaycanca](README.az.md) / [Кыргызча](README.ky.md) / [Тоҷикӣ](README.tg.md) / [Türkmençe](README.tk.md) / [O‘zbekcha](README.uz.md)

**An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes).** It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not.

Coverage includes all 15 former Soviet republics: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Archives are chosen by the event's historical jurisdiction and current record custodian; a regional example does not replace local research.

The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but **the agent talks to you in your language**: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on. It quotes sources in their original spelling with a translation, and builds search queries in the languages of the records.

---

## What it does

- **Case intake and scope.** One research question, known facts, who may be alive, what is off-limits.
- **Reproducible registers.** Persons, artifacts, claims, relationships and a full search log (CSV), plus a final report template.
- **Historical jurisdiction model.** It resolves every event to the state, province, district, parish or civil registry *as of the event date*, not today's map.
- **Name-variant matrices.** Pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish forms, patronymics, maiden names and transliterations.
- **Source strategy.** Originals first, then official catalogs, indexes, published document collections, and only then trees and forums as leads.
- **Evidence protocol.** Claims get explainable statuses, not percentages: `hypothesis`, `single-source`, `corroborated`, `strongly-corroborated`, `contradicted`, `unresolved`. Copies and mirrors of one record share an `independence_group`, so they never count as independent proof.
- **Identity resolution.** Namesakes stay separate `person_id`s until distinguishing evidence appears: house number, parents, godparents, exact birth date or military unit.
- **Audit script.** It checks referential integrity and flags weak corroboration before you write conclusions. An independence group counts only when a cited artifact belongs to it, so corroboration cannot be declared into existence. It also checks IDs and statuses in the working Markdown report, if present; the agent checks the delivered HTML against the registers. A summary shows what is still uncorroborated or marked illegible.
- **Institutional requests.** Draft and, when authorized, send focused requests to archives, libraries, universities and museums using available email or official web tools. If needed, offer a supported mail integration or a ready-to-send letter. Record the outcome, avoid duplicate sends and treat replies as evidence. See [correspondence guidance](references/correspondence.md).
- **Government services.** Choose an official civil-registration or archive request route, checking eligibility and how the result is delivered ([government portals](references/government-portals.md)).
- **Final report.** A complete HTML report is the default deliverable, with each relationship laid out edge by edge, contradictions, failed searches

description: One persona, many coding agents. Replace or inject system prompts across codex, claude, opencode, grok, omp, hermes, pi, zcode - with a local web console.
readme_excerpt:
# agent-purge

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/agent-purge)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-purge)
[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/ZiChuanLan/agent-purge)](https://github.com/ZiChuanLan/agent-purge/stargazers)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/agent-purge)](LICENSE)

一份系统提示词，喂给多个 coding agent。支持替换（replace）、只发人设（strict）、追加（append）、清空（off）四种模式，可热切换，全程可逆。

```
agent-purge web          # 本地控制台 http://127.0.0.1:7788
agent-purge codex        # 用当前 persona 启动 codex
agent-purge pi --ask "…" # 一次性提问
```

## 它做什么

每家 coding agent 读系统提示词的位置都不一样：有的认启动参数，有的认配置文件，有的只能靠插件改运行时对象。agent-purge 把这些入口统一成三件事：

| 通道 | 机制 | 生效范围 |
|---|---|---|
| `install` | 写入该 harness 的托管配置块（Markdown / hooks / 插件） | 常驻，别人启动也生效 |
| `shim` | 往 PATH 前置同名小壳，转发给 `agent-purge <h>` | 裸敲命令也接管 |
| `slash` | 会话内 `/purge on\|off\|status` | 热切换，不动磁盘 |

三层都写的是同一份 `personas/<id>.md` 的正文。`--mode off` 或 Web 总开关关掉时，全部撤回到原样——不留残渣。

## 安装

```bash
npm i -g agent-purge     # 或 npx agent-purge web
```

要求 Node ≥ 20，零依赖。

**用 magpie 网关？** 插件不在 npm 包里，在仓库的 `magpie-plugin/` 子目录——不要指向仓库根（根 `package.json` 是 CLI，只有 `bin`，magpie 会拒绝）：

```bash
magpie plugin add /path/to/agent-purge/magpie-plugin
```

首次使用先跑一次 `agent-purge web`（打开 http://127.0.0.1:7788 的控制台，先看/选一个人设；不想开界面就用 `agent-purge ls`），它会生成 `~/.agent-purge/personas/`；再跑 `node magpie-plugin/gen-personas.mjs` 生成 Persona 页的人设清单。

详见下文「magpie 网关插件（可选）」。

**数据独立存放**，升级不会被覆盖：默认 `~/.agent-purge/`（Windows `C:\Users\<你>\.agent-purge\`），里面是 `state.json` 和 `personas/`。想换位置就设环境变量：

```bash
export AGENT_PURGE_HOME=/path/to/your/data     # Windows: setx AGENT_PURGE_HOME D:\ap-data
```

旧版本（0.1.x）把数据放在包目录里，首次运行会自动搬到新家，原文件不动。

## 人设

`personas/<id>.md` = frontmatter + 正文。正文就是会被写进系统提示词的那一段。

frontmatter 用 `description` 写「说明」（Web 列表和 `agent-purge ls` 显示的就是它）；旧的 `desc` 仍然认，不会报错。可选 `order`（排序）、`harness` / `model`（匹配用）。Web 里只改名字和说明时会保留 frontmatter 的其它键，不整段重写。

```bash
agent-purge ls                 # 列出全部 persona，标出当前匹配的
agent-purge use <id>           # 切换当前 persona
agent-purge pi --persona <id>  # 只这一轮用别的
```

首次运行会在 `personas/` 下生成 `neutral.md` 起步模板。

## 支持情况

每个数字都是实测值：本地假 provider 抓真实请求体，不是估算。

| harness | 机制 | 实测版本 | 默认 system | 注入后 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `codex` | 启动参数 `-c model_instructions_file=` | 0.163.0 | 21,026 | 24 |
| `claude` | `--system-prompt-file` + 二进制补丁清残留身份句 | 2.1.304 | 6,379 | 156 |
| `grok` | `--system-prompt-override` | 1.0.62 | 5,146 | 21 |
| `omp` | 原生扩展：`before_agent_start` 改写 systemPrompt 数组，会话内 `/purge` 热切；`--ask` 仍走 `--system-prompt` | 17.4.2 | 34,511 | 10,106 |
| `hermes` | 临时 HOME 里替换 `SOUL.md` | 0.21.5 | 8,139 | 7,554 |
| `zcode` | UserPromptSubmit hook（user 角色）+ `customSystemPrompt` | 0.16.9 | 9,359 | 9,359 |
| `opencode` | cwd 下 `.opencode/plugin/*.ts` 原地改 `output.system` | 1.19.3 | 19,332 | 112 |
| `opencode2` | `plugins/agent-purge-v2.ts` 的 `ctx.session.hook("context")` | 0.0.0-beta-17823 | 8,279 | 3,189 |
| `dsh` | cordis 插件（三个 profile 各一份） | 0.2.1-rc.2 | 5,713 | 68 |
| `pi` | 原生扩展，会话内 `/purge` | — | — | — |
| `antigravity` | 等长替换二进制里的身份句 | 1.23.x | ≈20,498 | — |
| `codebuddy` | `--system-prompt-file` | 2.171.0 | — | — |
| `qoder` / `workbuddy` | 不支持（提示词在服务端） | — | — | — |

`opencode` 和 `opencode2` 是两个不同的 npm 包（`opencode-ai` 1.x 与 `@opencode/cli` 2.x），插件接口完全不同，各自独立支持。

`agent-purge ls` 和 Web 控制台显示的是**运行期真值**：每个 harness 有没有装、版本、注入层（SYS / USER）、三个通道各自可用性。`matrix.json` 里是静态能力表，两者冲突时以运行期为准。

闭源桌面端（提示词在服务端或二进制里）只做原样启动，不做任何注入——`agent-purge <h>` 会明确打印原因，不会假装生效。

### 常驻安装（install）

```bash
agent-purge install <h>      # 写进该 harness 自己的托管位置，别人启动也生效
agent-purge uninstall <h>    # 摘掉，按字节还原
```

dsh 是唯一有多个形态的：desktop / web / headless 共用一套 cordis 插件，装在各自 profile 的 `node_modules/agent-purge/`，并在 `cordis.patch.yml` 里 `- insert` 挂上，不改 `app.asar`。装完重启一次，之后热生效；三个形态还能在 Web 面板分别勾选。

## magpie 网关插件（可选）

[magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) 把各家 agent 的请求收进本地网关。挂上这个插件后，**凡是经过网关的请求**（Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode、pi…）的 system 段都按 agent-purge 的当前人设改写——不用逐个 harness 装，换人设也不用重启 magpie。

description: A free AI assistant and survival library that runs on your own computer, with no internet needed. Shows the source of every answer.
readme_excerpt:
# Survival LLM

A free AI assistant and survival library that runs entirely on your own computer and works with no
internet. Ask it how to keep food safe in a blackout, treat a burn or purify water: it searches an
offline library of medical, emergency, how-to and encyclopedia articles, answers from what it finds,
and shows you the exact passage each answer came from.

- **Offline and private.** The AI model and the library live on your computer. Your questions never leave it, and once set up it works with the internet off.
- **Shows its sources.** Every answer lists the articles it read; click one to read it yourself, cited passage highlighted, with its license. Ask "where did you get that?" and it opens the source.
- **Shows its reasoning.** Show reasoning, under each answer, opens what the AI thought before it answered, step by step, with the searches and articles it read in between. It stays hidden until you click it. How much it reasons is up to you: Reasoning, next to Send, is a budget (Off, 1,000, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens, or no limit), and at the limit its thinking stops and it answers from what it has.
- **Yours to adjust.** The Instructions button shows the instructions the AI gets before you ask anything (the app adds today's date, the names of your files and your Memory notes after them); edit them and Save to change how it answers (Reset brings back the original). The Length limit next to Send sets how long an answer may run, or turns the limit off.
- **Add your own files.** Your files, at the top, takes PDFs, Word documents, EPUB ebooks, web pages and text files (drop them on the window or choose them), so the AI can search your generator's manual, your medicines list or your family's emergency plan along with the library. They stay on your computer, in the `Survival LLM Files` folder in your home folder; files you put in that folder, or change there, are picked up on their own. It can't read scans or photos of pages yet.
- **Remembers you.** Tell it your daughter is allergic to penicillin or that you have a Honda generator, and it saves a short note so later chats know it too; each answer shows what it saved, with Undo. Memory, at the top, shows every note in one list you can edit, and a switch turns off the AI's saving (it still reads the notes you keep). The notes stay on your computer, in one plain text file with the app's settings.
- **Updates itself.** Check for updates, at the bottom of the window, looks for a new version (it also looks once a day while it runs, by fetching one small file from the project's web page; nothing about you is sent). Update now downloads it, checks it, and restarts into it, keeping your models, library, files and settings. Newer libraries are offered there too.
- **Built for emergencies.** About 1.5 million articles (500,000 in the smaller download): about 930,000 of Wikipedia's most-read articles, WikiMed, MedlinePlus, a UK medicines guide, WikEM, Ready.gov, CDC, U.S. military and FEMA survival and first-aid manuals, the USDA canning guide, risk references for estimating micromorts (life tables, U.S. death rates), wikiHow, iFixit, Appropedia, Energypedia and practical Q&A. See [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

## Install

Do this while you have internet. After that, it needs none. Setup takes 20 minutes to about 2½ hours, depending on
your computer and internet speed (the biggest AI model is 80 GB); you only click for about 5 minutes.

**Mac** (Apple Silicon, macOS 14 Sonoma or newer)
1. Download `Survival-LLM-mac.zip` and double-click it to unzip. Move **Survival LLM** to Applications if you like.
2. Double-click **Survival LLM**. The first time, macOS says it can't verify the app, because it isn't sold through
   Apple. Click **Done**, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down to "Survival LLM was blocked",
   click **Open Anyway**, and confirm with your password. You only do this once.

**Windows** (10 or 11, 64-bit)
1. Download `Survival-LLM-windows.zip`, right-click

description: Create Apple style dimensional drawings of UI components.
readme_excerpt:
dimensional-drawing ✏️📐

Give it a UI component, get back a one-page technical drawing of it.
Paddings, gaps, corner radii, layers and viewport placement, measured and labeled like Apple's dimensional drawings.

Install · Use it · Make it move · Examples

--- Apple publishes [dimensional drawings](https://developer.apple.com/accessories/dimensional-drawings/) for every device so accessory makers can build cases that fit. They are calm, dense and beautiful: one sheet, a few views, tiny detail circles, numbers everywhere. This repo teaches your agent to draw **your components** the same way. A card or a dialog becomes a spec sheet you could hand to anyone and they would rebuild its *architecture*: paddings, gaps, radii, layers, how it sits in the viewport. Copy and content are left out on purpose, so the drawing stays true when the text changes. ## What's inside 🎁 ``` skills/ ├── dimensional-drawing/ the drawing skill │ ├── SKILL.md │ └── examples/ card + dialog sheets (single HTML files) └── dimensional-drawing-motion/ turns a sheet into a ~10 s film ├── SKILL.md ├── templates/ reference scene + stylesheet └── adapters/ ├── claude-motion.md Claude's Motion artifact (primary) └── headless/ Playwright + ffmpeg, no Claude needed ``` ### The house rules | | | |---|---| | ⚫️ **Monochrome** | grays only; things are told apart by line weight, dashes and hatches | | 🧱 **Architecture, not content** | `TITLE SLOT · FLEX`, `ACTION · HUG`, `CONTENT SLOT · FILL` | | 🔤 **Variables, not numbers** | `S1`, `R2`, `H1 = 2·S1 + H3`, `R2 = R1 − B − S6` | | 🏷️ **Unbranded** | neutral names like `UI-CARD-001` | | 🙅 **Never invent values** | unknowns stay `[TBD]` | ## Install **Claude Code** ```bash git clone https://github.com/enesozturk/dimensional-drawing cp -r dimensional-drawing/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/ ``` **claude.ai / Claude desktop:** zip a skill folder (for example `skills/dimensional-drawing`) and add it under *Settings → Capabilities → Skills*. **Any other agent** (Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, …): use the [`skills`](https://skills.sh) CLI, or point your agent at the `SKILL.md` files. ```bash npx skills add enesozturk/dimensional-drawing ``` ## Use it Ask for a drawing and point at the source (a repo file, a Storybook story, a URL, a screenshot): > Make a dimensional drawing of the `Card` component in `src/components/Card.tsx` > Draw the anatomy of our settings dialog, same style as the examples You get a title block with the key variables on top, then one dense sheet: notes, plan view, exploded layers, detail views (nested corner, radii, body), and variable tables. It works for physical things too (third-angle views, mm, published specs only). Try a thermos 🫖. ## Make it move 🎬 The motion skill animates a finished sheet like a pen drawing it while a camera moves over the paper: 1. close-up on the header as its lines draw in 2. pull back to the plan view while the rest draws 3. layers lift off the plan into the exploded view (strokes first, fills after, so nothing flashes) 4. pull back to the full sheet as the remaining views draw in The scene is a pure function of time, so it runs in two places: | | | |---|---| | **With Claude** | ask *"animate this drawing"*. Claude builds it in the **Motion** artifact and you export MP4. This is the primary target and where the timing was tuned. | | **Without Claude** | `cd skills/dimensional-drawing-motion/adapters/headless && npm install`, then `node render.mjs --
